reconcile.connective: Gill distinguishes the moment of the call, when the land was unnamed (Genesis 12:1), from Genesis 12:5's account of Abram already en route to Canaan.

discrepancy.connective: William Henry Burr's 1860 pamphlet lists the pair outright as a contradiction, headlined 'Abraham departed to go into Canaan' vs. 'went not knowing where.'

skeptic.name: William Henry Burr
skeptic.attribution: William Henry Burr, Self-Contradictions of the Bible (1860), no. 92

excerpts.excerpt_text: for though he went forth to go into the land of Canaan, and into the land of Canaan he came, Gen 12:5, yet, when God called him to go forth, and he prepared to obey his call, he knew not what land he was to go into; for it is only said, Gen 12:1, unto a land that I will show thee …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly distinguishes the moment of the call (destination unnamed, Gen 12:1) from the later departure narrated in Gen 12:5 (Canaan already the known target), resolving the apparent knowledge conflict.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-1763), on Hebrews 11:7-8
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this exact tension directly, distinguishing Abram's ignorance at the call (Gen 12:1) from his known destination by the time of the Gen 12:5 departure.

link.title: Hebrews 11:8—Did Abraham know where he was going when he left his homeland to follow God?
